text:
alex: Heads-up — Escalation from Acme. Batch rerank is returning a flat list of scores that don't map back to per-query candidate lists when queries have different candidate counts. No HTTP error (200 OK) but results are semantically wrong. Customer calls it a production blocker. @maria can you take?

maria: Thanks. Any request_id, SDK version, or a minimal repro payload?

alex: Request id req_0x9f3a. SDK python client v0.42.1. No HTTP errors, just wrong mapping. Server log excerpt: `rerank: candidate_index_mismatch detected, expected mapping length 4 got 5` — weird. Payload snippet: ```json
{"queries": [{"id": "q1", "candidates": ["A"]}, {"id": "q2", "candidates": ["B", "C", "D"]}], "model": "rerank-small"}
```

maria: Can you repro locally with curl? Also paste the response you saw.

alex: Repro steps: curl works for me. Example: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank/batch \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"queries":[{"candidates":["A"]},{"candidates":["B","C","D"]}] }'
``` Response body we got: ```json
{"scores": [0.9, 0.12, 0.6, 0.3]}
``` Which is ambiguous — client expected per-query grouping: `[[0.9], [0.12,0.6,0.3]]` but the API returned a flat array without explicit offsets. The client lib tried to reconstruct using per_query_counts but mapping ended up wrong for this customer.

devon: Sounds like a serialization/parsing mismatch between how the client encodes per-query candidate lists and how the server decodes them. Particularly suspicious when a query only has one candidate — we sometimes take a fast path that flattens arrays.

maria: Do we have metrics for this request? Any server-side counters (flattened_counts / per_query_counts) for req_0x9f3a?

alex: metric dump: flattened_counts=4, per_query_counts=[1,3], scores_length=4. Log also shows the customer sent NDJSON variant originally (they said they stream candidate lists newline-delimited). They mentioned sending a trailing newline at the end of the payload.

mike: I can reproduce when I send NDJSON with a trailing newline. Our NDJSON parser treats the final newline as an empty record in some SDK versions, which becomes an extra empty candidate or causes off-by-one in offsets calculation. Validator later collapses but offsets stay off.

maria: Good find. Workaround to give customer now?

alex: Quick workaround: send a single JSON array payload (Content-Type: application/json) instead of NDJSON; ensure no trailing newline. Also validate the client-side library version — older SDKs (<=0.42.1) had a bug in ndjson concat.

devon: I'll push a hotfix: 1) server-side defensive validation to compare sum(per_query_candidate_counts) against total candidates and raise a 400 with a clear message if mismatch; 2) fix NDJSON parser to ignore empty lines; 3) add unit/regression tests. Creating PR now, ETA ~3 hours. I'll also add an alert metric candidate_count_skew for any future occurrences.

mike: Also add a regression test that sends mixed single-candidate + multi-candidate queries with NDJSON + trailing newline to catch this.

maria: Action items: (1) alex — contact customer with workaround + ask for exact payload they used, (2) devon — PR + patch + tests, (3) mike — help with test cases and add server telemetry, (4) I'll draft a postmortem template after fix.

alex: On it. I'll reply to the customer with the workaround and ask for the raw bytes. Will update this thread when they confirm. :thumbsup:
